Broad participation (75% advancing) with IBM-led cap-weighted lift, but conviction soft — sub-average volume suggests rotational rather than fresh accumulation.
Strong breadth and magnitude, but rel-volume 0.13 is a red flag — drift higher with no institutional footprint. Treat with caution.

sector_breadth_notes.note: Tech leadership is concentrated — all three qualifying industries sit in XLK, led by Computer Hardware's AI-infrastructure surge. IT Services and Solar follow with weaker conviction.
Consumer Discretionary qualifying at sector level but no industries pass gate — Apparel Mfg, RVs, Packaging, Apparel Retail all deeply red. Sector strength is narrow/megacap-driven.
Materials sector qualified but Steel and Building Materials are bottom laggards — sector lift must be coming from non-qualifying industries (chemicals/metals) below the gate.
Industrials weak under the hood — Railroads (0% advancing) and Staffing rank among worst industries. Sector ETF strength is masking poor internals.
Real Estate qualifying but REIT-Retail collapsing (9% advancing). Strength is concentrated outside retail REITs — likely data center / industrial REITs.
Communications qualifying but Broadcasting is a major laggard. Sector lift is megacap-driven (likely interactive media), not broad-based.

key_divergences: Severe — sector-level breadth says 7 sectors qualifying, but only 3 industries (all XLK) clear the gate. Most qualifying sectors are megacap-ETF driven while their industry internals (Steel, Railroads, REIT-Retail, Apparel) are deeply red.
leadership_theme: AI hardware leads alone; broader sector strength is megacap-ETF illusion masking weak industry breadth
